subproblem.title: Evaluation of a finite-mass current is bounded by mass times the coefficient sup norm (Simon 6.2.4; supplied proof step 3)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with M(X) ≠ ∞, ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and c ∈ ℝ with c > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ c for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then |X(ω)| ≤ c·M(X)^ℝ, where M(X)^ℝ := M(X).toReal. Conventions: 𝒟ⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n is the real submodule of smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞) n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ⊆ U, and ω(x) denotes (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x; |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of an n-covector α (e the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P) and ‖α‖ its operator norm as a continuous alternating map; 𝒟_n(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U n is the space of n-currents in U (an ℝ-linear map toCurrent : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ, applied as X(ω), together with sequential continuity: X(ω_j) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0); M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, i.e. over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ U and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → X.mass ≠ ∞ → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ c) → |X ω| ≤ c * X.mass.toReal
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the supplied proof of cmc_fc_series_current; Simon Ch. 6, (2.4) M(T) = sup_{|ω| ≤ 1, ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U)} T(ω) (chapter-06.txt lines 220–226), which gives |T(ω)| ≤ |ω|·M(T), the estimate Simon uses for the M-absolutely convergent series in the proof of 7.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 2119–2123). Notation: N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ω(x) := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x; M := X.mass ∈ [0, ∞] and M^ℝ := M.toReal. Hypotheses: c > 0, M ≠ ∞, and N(ω(x)) ≤ c for every x ∈ ℝ^P. The sibling theorem norm_props is Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props; only its conjunct (ii) (N(t·α) = |t|·N(α)) is used.
1. (Admissible rescalings.) Let s ∈ ℝ with |s| = c⁻¹. Since TestFormOn U n is a real submodule, s•ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, and its membership gives tsupport (s•ω) ⊆ U. As a form, (s•ω)(x) = s•ω(x) for every x (the submodule coercion commutes with scalar multiplication; this holds definitionally). By norm_props (ii), N((s•ω)(x)) = |s|·N(ω(x)) = c⁻¹·N(ω(x)) ≤ c⁻¹·c = 1, using N(ω(x)) ≤ c and c⁻¹ ≥ 0. Hence s•ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U (tsupport ⊆ U and N ≤ 1 everywhere).
2. (Evaluation bounded by mass.) By SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ENNReal.ofReal (X(s•ω)) ≤ X.massOn U, and X.massOn U = X.mass = M by the definition of mass. Since M ≠ ∞, ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal turns this into X(s•ω) ≤ M^ℝ.
3. (Linearity.) X(s•ω) = s·X(ω), because X.toCurrent is ℝ-linear (map_smul, smul_eq_mul). Hence s·X(ω) ≤ M^ℝ for every s ∈ ℝ with |s| = c⁻¹.
4. (Both signs.) Since c > 0, |c⁻¹| = c⁻¹ and |−c⁻¹| = c⁻¹. Step 3 with s = c⁻¹ gives c⁻¹·X(ω) ≤ M^ℝ; multiplying by c > 0 gives X(ω) ≤ c·M^ℝ. Step 3 with s = −c⁻¹ gives −c⁻¹·X(ω) ≤ M^ℝ; multiplying by c gives −X(ω) ≤ c·M^ℝ. By abs_le, |X(ω)| ≤ c·M^ℝ = c·X.mass.toReal. ∎
Lean note (a compiled route, about 35 lines): for admissibility use `refine ⟨(s • ω).property.2, fun x => ?_⟩` and `have hx : ((s • ω : TestFormOn U n) : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x = s • ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) := rfl`, then `rw [hx, hhom, hs]` and `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left`, `inv_mul_cancel₀`; `X.le_massOn hadm : ENNReal.ofReal (X (s • ω)) ≤ X.massOn U` is accepted at type `≤ X.mass` by definitional unfolding; `rw [ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal hX] at h1`; `rw [map_smul, smul_eq_mul]` for X (s • ω) = s * X ω; finish with `abs_le`, `field_simp` and `linarith`.
proof_key_steps: For |s| = c⁻¹, s•ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) has tsupport ⊆ U and |s•ω(x)| = c⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ 1 (norm_props (ii)), so it is admissible for M = M_U.
GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn and M ≠ ∞ give X(s•ω) ≤ M.toReal.

audit.reason: The prose and type contain all required hypotheses, particularly c>0 and finite mass. Homogeneity makes both signed rescalings admissible, le_massOn bounds their evaluations, and finite mass justifies conversion to toReal. Linearity and multiplication by positive c yield both inequalities required for the absolute-value bound. No series-current theorem is used.

subproblem.title: A linear functional on test forms dominated by the coefficient sup norm is a current (supplied proof step 7; the bound of step 6 is its hypothesis)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, L : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ an ℝ-linear map (TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) and A ∈ ℝ such that |L(ω)| ≤ c·A whenever ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), c ∈ ℝ, c > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ c for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then there is a current Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Y(ω) = L(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Conventions: 𝒟ⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n is the real submodule of smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞) n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ⊆ U, and ω(x) denotes (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x; |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of an n-covector α (e the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P) and ‖α‖ its operator norm as a continuous alternating map; 𝒟_n(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U n is the space of n-currents in U (an ℝ-linear map toCurrent : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ, applied as X(ω), together with sequential continuity: X(ω_j) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0); M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, i.e. over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ U and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (L : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (A : ℝ), (∀ (ω : TestFormOn U n) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ c) → |L ω| ≤ c * A) → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Y ω = L ω
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the supplied proof of cmc_fc_series_current, whose step-6 bound is the hypothesis (H) below (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2: the M-absolutely convergent series "define" currents, chapter-06.txt lines 2119–2123; the topology of 𝒟ⁿ(U), chapter-06.txt lines 170–176). This isolates the fact that a linear functional bounded by A·sup_x |ω(x)| is sequentially continuous, i.e. a current. Notation: N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ω(x) := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x; ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Covector (Euclid P) n. Hypothesis (H): |L(ω)| ≤ c·A whenever ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), c > 0 and N(ω(x)) ≤ c for all x. Sibling theorems: norm_props = Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props (only conjunct (iii) is used) and uniform_small = Submission.dpf_pfc_testFormOnConverges_zero_uniform.
1. (A ≥ 0.) Apply (H) to ω = 0 and c = 1. The zero test form has N(0(x)) = N(0) = 0 ≤ 1 (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm_zero), and L(0) = 0 by linearity, so 0 = |L(0)| ≤ 1·A = A.
2. (The constant C.) By norm_props (iii) applied to P and n, there is C ∈ ℝ with C ≥ 0 and N(α) ≤ C·‖α‖ for every α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n.
3. (Sequential continuity of L.) Let ωs : ℕ → 𝒟ⁿ(U) with TestFormOnConverges ωs 0. By uniform_small (applied to P, n, U, ωs), for every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large j, ‖ωs_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all x. Let η > 0 and put ε := η / (2(C + 1)(A + 1)); then ε > 0, since η > 0, C + 1 ≥ 1 and A + 1 ≥ 1 (steps 1–2). Choose j₀ with ‖ωs_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all j ≥ j₀ and all x. For j ≥ j₀ and every x, N(ωs_j(x)) ≤ C·‖ωs_j(x)‖ ≤ C·ε ≤ (C + 1)·ε, using C ≥ 0 and ε > 0. Since (C + 1)·ε > 0, (H) with c := (C + 1)·ε gives |L(ωs_j)| ≤ (C + 1)·ε·A. Now (C + 1)·ε·(A + 1) = η/2, and (C + 1)·ε > 0 with A ≤ A + 1, so (C + 1)·ε·A ≤ (C + 1)·ε·(A + 1) = η/2 < η. Hence dist(L(ωs_j), 0) = |L(ωs_j)| < η for all j ≥ j₀. Since η > 0 was arbitrary, L(ωs_j) → 0 as j → ∞ (Metric.tendsto_atTop). (This is the estimate of step 7 of the supplied proof, |Y(ω_k)| ≤ (N·ε_k + 1/(k+1))·s → 0, written with an explicit ε and j₀.)
4. (The current.) A GeometricCurrentOn U n is a structure with fields toCurrent : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ and continuous' : for every ωs with TestFormOnConverges ωs 0, toCurrent(ωs_j) → 0 in ℝ. Step 3 is exactly continuous' for toCurrent := L. Put Y := ⟨L, step 3⟩. Its coercion to a function is Y.toCurrent = L, so Y(ω) = L(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (definitionally). ∎
Lean note (a compiled route, about 30 lines): `obtain ⟨C, hC0, hC⟩ := (hnorm P n).2.2.1`; `have hA : 0 ≤ A := by simpa using hL 0 1 one_pos (fun x => by simp)`; `refine ⟨⟨L, fun ωs hωs => ?_⟩, fun ω => rfl⟩`; `obtain ⟨K, -, -, -, hunif⟩ := hsmall P n U ωs hωs`; `rw [Metric.tendsto_atTop]`; `set ε : ℝ := η / (2 * (C + 1) * (A + 1))`; `obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := eventually_atTop.mp (hunif ε hεpos)`; bound N(ωs_j(x)) with `hC`, `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left` and `nlinarith`; `rw [Real.dist_eq, sub_zero]`; `field_simp` proves (C + 1) * ε * (A + 1) = η / 2, and `nlinarith` closes (C + 1) * ε * A < η.
proof_key_steps: (H) at ω = 0, c = 1 gives A ≥ 0; norm_props (iii) gives C ≥ 0 with |α| ≤ C‖α‖.
If ωs → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U), uniform_small gives eventually ‖ωs_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all x, hence |ωs_j(x)| ≤ (C + 1)ε.
(H) gives |L(ωs_j)| ≤ (C + 1)εA ≤ η/2 < η for ε = η/(2(C + 1)(A + 1)), so L(ωs_j) → 0.
Y := ⟨L, continuity⟩ is a current with Y(ω) = L(ω).

subproblem.title: A test form has bounded Euclidean coefficient norm (Simon 6.1.15; supplied proof step 2)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Then there is a real number c > 0 such that |ω(x)| ≤ c for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Conventions: 𝒟ⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n is the real submodule of smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞) n-forms on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ⊆ U, and ω(x) denotes (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x; |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of an n-covector α (e the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P) and ‖α‖ its operator norm as a continuous alternating map; 𝒟_n(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U n is the space of n-currents in U (an ℝ-linear map toCurrent : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ, applied as X(ω), together with sequential continuity: X(ω_j) → 0 whenever TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0); M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, i.e. over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ U and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U n), ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ c
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the supplied proof of cmc_fc_series_current (Simon Ch. 6, (1.15): |ω| = sup_x |ω(x)| is finite for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), chapter-06.txt lines 170–178). Notation: N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α; for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), ω(x) := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x. The sibling theorem norm_props is Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props; only its conjunct (iv) (continuity of N) is used.
1. (Regularity of ω.) By definition of the submodule TestFormOn U n, ω ∈ TestFormOn U n means IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ U, where IsTestForm ω = IsSmoothForm ω ∧ HasCompactSupport ω and IsSmoothForm ω = ContDiff ℝ ∞ ω. A C^∞ map is continuous (ContDiff.continuous), so x ↦ ω(x) is a continuous map ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) n with compact support.
2. (The function g.) Put g(x) := N(ω(x)). By norm_props (iv) applied to P and n, α ↦ N(α) is continuous, so g = N ∘ ω is continuous. Since N(0) = 0 (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm_zero), g(x) = 0 whenever ω(x) = 0; hence g has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_left with g 0 = 0).
3. (Boundedness.) A continuous real-valued function with compact support is bounded (Mathlib Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support): there is C ∈ ℝ with ‖g(x)‖ ≤ C for every x. Since ‖g(x)‖ = |g(x)| ≥ g(x), we get g(x) ≤ C for every x.
4. (A positive bound.) Put c := max(C, 0) + 1. Then c ≥ 1 > 0, and g(x) ≤ C ≤ max(C, 0) < c for every x ∈ ℝ^P, i.e. N(ω(x)) ≤ c for all x. This c witnesses the claim. ∎
Lean note (a compiled route, about 15 lines): `have hsmooth : IsSmoothForm (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) := ω.property.1.1`; `(hnorm P n).2.2.2.comp (ContDiff.continuous hsmooth)` (IsSmoothForm unfolds definitionally to ContDiff ℝ ∞; do not `open scoped ContDiff`, which turns `ω` into a reserved token); `HasCompactSupport.comp_left (g := covectorEuclideanNorm) ω.property.1.2 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero P n)`; `obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hcont.bounded_above_of_compact_support hcs`; `refine ⟨max C 0 + 1, by positivity, fun x => ?_⟩`; finish with `Real.norm_eq_abs`, `le_abs_self`, `le_max_left` and `linarith`.
proof_key_steps: ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is ContDiff ℝ ∞, hence continuous, and has compact support.
x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous (norm_props (iv)) and has compact support because |0| = 0.
A continuous compactly supported real function is bounded by some C.
c := max(C, 0) + 1 > 0 bounds |ω(x)| for all x.

audit.reason: The proposition exactly states the positive global coefficient bound. Smoothness gives continuity; norm_props gives continuity of the coefficient norm; its value at zero preserves compact support. The cited boundedness lemma then supplies C, and max(C,0)+1 is a positive bound. Only the declared norm_props dependency is needed.
